posts.name: Rakshitha P
posts.cooked:
In system commands,I had to do one BPT which is like compulsory for attending oppe but in that I had to work with a file script.sh for which several swap files have been created and it is present in readonly form as well I couldn’t modify or write in it..What should I do to alter it?I couldn’t remove the swap files as well as it shows permission denied. I couldn’t use sudo command also.

IMG-20260321-WA00061920×3413 1.05 MB

posts.name: Ishan Shishodiya
posts.cooked:
Vim creates swap files as a safety mechanism. So if your session ever crashes unexpectedly, you’d not lose out on your progress. In your case it must have happened that a previous vim session crashed unexpectedly without properly closing the file.

You have two swap files right now, /var/tmp/script.sh.swp and /tmp/script.sh.swp, so you can try deleting those and reopen script.sh.

rm /var/tmp/script.sh.swp
rm /tmp/script.sh.swp
vim script.sh

posts.name: Ishan Shishodiya
posts.cooked:
I assumed that the user would own the swap file, but if the root user is owning that then yeah deleting it won’t be possible. From the screenshot it seems that one of the swap files is owned by 23f2002876 and not you.

You can try clicking (D)elete or (E)dit when the prompt shows up in vim about what to do. Can you please mention which assignment is this?

Another thing I see from your terminal title is that you’re inside /opt/se2001/BPT3_problem_1. If so then switch to ~/se2001/BPT3_problem_1 instead.

posts.name: Rakshitha P
posts.cooked: BPT3 for all the problems I couldn’t modify script.sh and clicking D or E in vim is also not working after inserting when I give escape and :wq it shows writing permission is denied

posts.name: Ishan Shishodiya
posts.cooked:
Yes, that’s because you’re inside /opt/se2001 instead of ~/se2001. Do

cd ~/se2001

and then create/go to your BPT3 directory.

cd ~
cd se2001

cd BPT3_problem_1

You should be able to see Ques1 of BPT3, you can do for other ques as well.
